newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Exchange to simplify index figures.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Exchange to simplify index figures.

text.p: Istanbul's Stock Exchange said on Monday it would drop two zeros from current indices from January 2, 1997 for simplification purposes as several new indices will be introduced at the beginning of 1997.
The December 27 closing value of the composite IMKB-100 index would be divided by 100 to have a 1986 base value of one instead of the previous 100, the Exchange said in a press release.
December 27 closes of the industrial and financial indices will also be divided by 100 to have (Dec 31, 1990 = 33) base values instead of (Dec 31, 1990 = 3,255.75).
The IMKB-100 which closed at an all-time high of 97,588.80 on Friday and which will be replaced by the IMKB national-100 index from Thursday will have an opening value of 976.
The industrial index which ended at 104,590.85 on Friday and which will be changed to IMKB national-industrial from Thursday will open at 1,046.
The financial index which finished last week at 91,446.88 and which will be named IMKB national-financial from Thursday will open at 914.

The Exchange decided earlier this month to launch new indices from January 2 due to the rise in the number of listed firms in 1996 and the need to cover existing markets and sectors and a planned futures markets separately.

The new IMKB national-all which will include all shares except investment trusts will open at 976 on Thursday when the stock market reopens after an extended new year holiday which started from Friday.
The new IMKB national-30 to be used in a futures market planned to be launched next year will have an opening value of 976 on Thursday as well.

The new IMKB national-services index which will cover utilities, transportation, tourism and trade sectors will open at 1,046 on Thursday. Separate indices to be introduced for the four sub-sectors will also open at 1,046.

Sub-sectoral indices for food-beverages, textile-leather, forestry-paper-publishing, chemicals-petroleum-plastics, soil-based, metal, metalware-machinery industries classified under the IMKB national-industrial will each open at 1,046.
Sub-sectoral indices for banking, insurance, leasing-factoring and holding-investment sectors classified under the IMKB national-financial will each open at 914.
A separate index for investments trusts will be introduced on Thursday with an opening value of 976.
New indices representing the Exchange's regional and new company markets will also open at 976 on Thursday.

Of the above, only the main IMKB national-100, IMKB national-industrial, IMKB national-services and IMKB national-financial will be broadcast during trade hours while the others will be disclosed at the end of the sessions.
The Exchange will stop the calculation of indices according to weighted average share prices. The calculation will be made only according to closing prices from 1997.
